figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of the matched LLM/VLM alignment pipeline. (a) Data acquisition. Participants read sentences from five articles, one at a time, while concurrent eye-tracking and whole-cortex fMRI are recorded. (b) Attention feature extraction. Layer-wise self-attention matrices are extracted from each model, mapped from the token level to the word level, and the strict lower triangle is retained as the feature representation. (c) Model-human alignment. Lower-triangular attention features are used as predictors in ridge regression models targeting vertex-wise fMRI responses and human regressive saccades during natural reading; model alignment is evaluated within pairs as VLM minus LLM. (d) A visual-strength-conditioned analysis tests whether the VLM–LLM alignment difference scales with sentence-level visual semantic content.

Figure 2: Global fMRI alignment of different LLM–VLM pairs. Significant brain clusters from the single-modelto-brain correlation coefficients and from the contrast of VLM to LLM. Colored regions denote vertex-wise mean effect sizes across subjects. The contrasts are small and do not support a broad whole-cortex fMRI advantage for VLMs during natural reading.

Figure 3: Eye-movement alignment for regressive saccades. Mean normalized subject-level best-layer R2 by model. Gray points show individual subjects, and thin lines connect each subject’s LLM and VLM values within a pair. Asterisks represent significant LLM– VLM differences within a pair on two-sided paired ttests. Qwen2-VL and DeepSeek-VL show modest gains over their matched LLMs, whereas Idefics2 does not outperform Mistral.

Figure 4: Visual strength modulation of VLM–LLM alignment across matched model pairs. (a) Mean advantage in low-visual-strength and high-visual-strength conditions for three matched LLM/VLM pairs. Gray lines connect the same subjects across conditions; hollow bars denote group means ± SEM across subjects; dots denote individual subjects. (b) Visual-strength modulation index H = Ahigh − Alow for each model pair. Asterisks denote paired comparisons with p < .05. (c) Cortical localization maps. Surface projections show vertex-wise mean H in regions passing a one-sided cluster-mass sign-flip permutation test with cluster-forming threshold p = .01, cluster-level α = .05, and 10,000 permutations. Colored regions denote effect magnitude within significant clusters, highlighting targeted involvement of lateral temporal and inferior parietal semantic networks.
Table 1: Configurations of the LLMs and VLMs evaluated in this study.

Figure 5: Subject-level LLM–VLM consistency for eye-movement alignment. Each point represents one participant; the x-axis shows the LLM alignment score and the y-axis shows the VLM alignment score within the same matched pair.
Figure 6: Subject-level LLM–VLM consistency for fMRI alignment. Format follows Figure 5.
Figure 8: System prompt used for LLM-based visual strength scoring. The same prompt was used for all three judges.
Figure 9: User prompt used for LLM-based visual strength scoring. The placeholder {sentence} was replaced with the target sentence at inference time.
